original_query: select  count(*) from (     select distinct c_last_name, c_first_name, d_date     from store_sales, date_dim, customer           where store_sales.ss_sold_date_sk = date_dim.d_date_sk       and store_sales.ss_customer_sk = customer.c_customer_sk       and d_month_seq between 1198 and 1198 + 11       and c_birth_month in (1, 3, 4, 6)       and ss_list_price between 185 and 244       and ss_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 80 AND 100   intersect     select distinct c_last_name, c_first_name, d_date     from catalog_sales, date_dim, customer           where catalog_sales.cs_sold_date_sk = date_dim.d_date_sk       and catalog_sales.cs_bill_customer_sk = customer.c_customer_sk       and d_month_seq between 1198 and 1198 + 11       and c_birth_month in (1, 3, 4, 6)       and cs_list_price between 185 and 244       and cs_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 80 AND 100   intersect     select distinct c_last_name, c_first_name, d_date     from web_sales, date_dim, customer           where web_sales.ws_sold_date_sk = date_dim.d_date_sk       and web_sales.ws_bill_customer_sk = customer.c_customer_sk       and d_month_seq between 1198 and 1198 + 11       and c_birth_month in (1, 3, 4, 6)       and ws_list_price between 185 and 244       and ws_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 80 AND 100 ) hot_cust limit 100;
rewritten_query:
WITH channel_customers AS (
    SELECT 'store' AS channel, c.c_last_name, c.c_first_name, d.d_date
    FROM store_sales ss
    JOIN date_dim d ON ss.ss_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
    JOIN customer c ON ss.ss_customer_sk = c.c_customer_sk
    WHERE d.d_month_seq BETWEEN 1198 AND 1209
      AND c.c_birth_month IN (1, 3, 4, 6)
      AND ss.ss_list_price BETWEEN 185 AND 244
      AND ss.ss_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 80 AND 100

    UNION ALL

    SELECT 'catalog', c.c_last_name, c.c_first_name, d.d_date
    FROM catalog_sales cs
    JOIN date_dim d ON cs.cs_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
    JOIN customer c ON cs.cs_bill_customer_sk = c.c_customer_sk
    WHERE d.d_month_seq BETWEEN 1198 AND 1209
      AND c.c_birth_month IN (1, 3, 4, 6)
      AND cs.cs_list_price BETWEEN 185 AND 244
      AND cs.cs_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 80 AND 100

    UNION ALL

    SELECT 'web', c.c_last_name, c.c_first_name, d.d_date
    FROM web_sales ws
    JOIN date_dim d ON ws.ws_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
    JOIN customer c ON ws.ws_bill_customer_sk = c.c_customer_sk
    WHERE d.d_month_seq BETWEEN 1198 AND 1209
      AND c.c_birth_month IN (1, 3, 4, 6)
      AND ws.ws_list_price BETWEEN 185 AND 244
      AND ws.ws_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 80 AND 100
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS hot_cust_count
FROM (
    SELECT c_last_name, c_first_name, d_date
    FROM channel_customers
    GROUP BY c_last_name, c_first_name, d_date
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT channel) = 3
) hot_cust;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Replace the chained INTERSECT over three DISTINCT branches with a UNION ALL of channel-tagged rows plus GROUP BY/HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT channel)=3. This emulates the three-way intersection in a single aggregation and avoids multiple sort/Unique/SetOp nodes. Rewrite score: 9/10 — this is the most impactful change.
Remove the outer LIMIT 100: it applies after COUNT(*), which always returns one row, so it has no effect on the result. Rewrite score: 1/10.
Remove redundant SELECT DISTINCT in the INTERSECT operands: INTERSECT already returns distinct rows; the rewrite using GROUP BY makes it unnecessary. Rewrite score: 3/10.
Fold the constant expression `1198 + 11` into `1209`. Rewrite score: 2/10.
Rewrite implicit comma joins as explicit ANSI JOINs for readability and to make join order clearer to maintain. Rewrite score: 2/10 (readability, not performance).

Optional physical tuning (not a query rewrite): consider composite indexes such as sales(sold_date_sk, list_price, wholesale_cost, customer_sk), customer(c_customer_sk, c_birth_month, c_last_name, c_first_name), and date_dim(d_month_seq, d_date_sk). Rewrite score: 6/10 — test with real data before applying.
